_meta.note: Fixture data for the Agentic Project Visualizer. Uses MongoDB Extended JSON v2 (mongoexport --jsonFormat=canonical) so `mongoimport --jsonArray` recreates ObjectId and Date types correctly. Handpicked ObjectIds so cross-references are readable at a glance: 0*=users, 1*=models, 2*=prompts, 3*=tools, 4*=agents, 5*=workflows, 6*=files.

prompts.name: research_agent_system
prompts.content: You are a research agent. Use the provided tools to answer the user's question. Cite every fact you use. Never fabricate URLs.

prompts.name: writer_agent_system
prompts.content: You are a writing agent. Draft long-form content grounded in the retrieved index. Match the requested tone. Every claim must be traceable to a source.

prompts.content: You coordinate specialized sub-agents. Decide which sub-agent should handle the task, hand off the input verbatim, and combine their outputs into a single response.

prompts.content: Extract structured JSON matching the schema. No prose.

prompts.content: Classify the input text sentiment as positive, neutral, or negative.

prompts.content: Given a transaction, flag suspicious patterns. Be conservative.

prompts.name: content_moderator
prompts.content: Flag content violating: hate, violence, sexual, self-harm categories.

prompts.name: citation_verifier_system

prompts.name: code_documenter

prompts.name: dependency_upgrader

tools.name: missing_impl_tool
tools.description: DISTRACTOR: this tool references a function that does not exist in the codebase. The L2 scanner should surface it as an unresolved edge, NOT crash.

tools.name: phantom_module_tool
tools.description: DISTRACTOR: this tool references a MODULE that does not exist in the codebase (src.integrations.nonexistent). The L2 scanner should report a 'module not found' warning against this tool, NOT crash and NOT silently drop it. Pair with missing_impl_tool which exercises the 'function not found in module' branch.

tools.name: moved_tool
tools.description: L2 FALLBACK EXERCISE: this tool's module_path points at an old location the code has moved out of. Direct dotted-path lookup fails; the codebase-wide name search finds it under src/skills/. Proves L2 doesn't require tool code to live in a folder named 'tools' or a file named '*_tools.py'.
